subtitle: Learn how different chords can serve the same harmonic function while adding sophistication

backLink.label: Back to Chord Theory in Songs

introduction.title: The Art of Harmonic Choice
introduction.text: Chord substitution is like having a vocabulary of synonyms in music. When you know that several different chords can serve the same harmonic function, you can choose the one that best fits the emotional color and voice leading you want.

columns.title: Emotional Color
columns.text: Same function, different feeling: vi feels nostalgic, iii feels uncertain, both can replace I

columns.title: Voice Leading
columns.text: Choose substitutions that create smoother connections between chords

columns.title: Sophistication
columns.text: Transform simple progressions into more interesting harmonic journeys

cards.title: Tonic Function
cards.description: Chords that feel stable and at rest
items: I ↔ vi (most common)
I → iii (less stable)
vi → iii (minor to minor)

cards.title: Subdominant Function
cards.description: Chords that move away from home
items: IV ↔ ii (both very common)
IV → bVII (rock/modal sound)
ii → bVII (darker color)

cards.title: Dominant Function
cards.description: Chords that create tension and want to resolve
items: V ↔ V7 (add tension)
V7 ↔ bII7 (tritone sub)
V → vii° (leading tone emphasis)

cards.title: Relative Substitution
cards.description: Replace a chord with its relative major/minor
items: I (C) → vi (Am): Share two common tones (C-E)
vi (Am) → I (C): Brightens minor with major
IV (F) → ii (Dm): Both serve subdominant function

cards.title: Tritone Substitution
cards.description: Replace dominant chord with another dominant a tritone away
items: G7 (V7) → Db7 (bII7): Same tritone interval (B-F), different root
D7 (V7/V) → Ab7 (bII7/V): Chromatic bass movement

cards.title: Circle of Fifths
cards.description: Replace chord with one a 5th away that shares function
items: IV (F) → bVII (Bb): Both move away from tonic
vi (Am) → iii (Em): Parallel motion down the circle

cards.title: Diminished Passing
cards.description: Use diminished chords between diatonic chords
items: I-ii (C-Dm) → I-#idim-ii (C-C#dim-Dm): Chromatic bass line C-C#-D
vi-V (Am-G) → vi-#vidim-V (Am-A#dim-G): Smooth voice leading

cards.title: "Let It Be" - Verse
cards.description: Original: C - G - Am - F (I - V - vi - IV)
items: Replace vi with iii: C - G - Em - F (Em is less stable than Am, creates more forward motion)
Replace IV with ii: C - G - Am - Dm (Dm is darker than F, more melancholic feeling)
Add diminished passing: C - G - Am - A#dim - F/Bb (A#dim creates chromatic bass line A-A#-Bb)

cards.title: "Yesterday" - Bridge
cards.description: Original: Em - A7 - Dm - G7 (iii - VI7 - ii - V7)
items: Tritone substitute A7: Em - Eb7 - Dm - G7 (Eb7 replaces A7, creates chromatic bass movement)
Replace iii with I: C - A7 - Dm - G7 (C major brighter than Em, changes emotional color)

cards.title: Jazz Substitutions
items: ii-V-I becomes: ii-bII7-I (Tritone substitute creates chromatic bass movement)
Dominant chains: VII7-III7-VI7-II7-V7-I (Each dominant resolves down a 5th)
Diminished passing: Abundant use between any two chords (Creates sophisticated harmonic rhythm)

cards.title: Pop/Rock Substitutions
items: Modal interchange: bVII, bVI, bIII from parallel minor (Adds darkness and modal flavor)
Relative substitutions: I ↔ vi most common (Emotional contrast without losing function)
Power chord movement: Focus on bass line motion (Function less important than melodic bass)

sections.title: How to Choose the Right Substitution

cards.title: Consider These Factors
items: 1. Voice Leading: Does it create smoother connections?
2. Emotional Color: Does it match the lyrical content?
3. Genre Expectations: What sounds natural in this style?
4. Melody Support: Does it support the vocal melody?

cards.title: Decision Framework
items: Start with function: What job does this chord need to do?
Consider context: What chords come before and after?
Test alternatives: Try different options and trust your ears
Remember the melody: Some substitutions clash with vocal lines
Serve the song: Sophistication should enhance, not distract

exercises.title: Beginner Practice
items: Practice I-vi-IV-V with different tonic substitutions
Replace IV with ii in simple progressions
Try vi instead of I at the end of phrases
Learn to hear functional equivalents

exercises.title: Advanced Practice
items: Practice tritone substitutions in ii-V-I progressions
Add diminished passing chords to standards
Reharmonize simple songs with complex substitutions
Analyze jazz standards for substitution patterns
